stem: A nightly reporting job calls the Messages API and retries every 429 with exponential backoff. Since this morning, every request has failed with 429 rate_limit_error. The responses have no retry-after header, the error details show enforced_spend_limit_reached, and traffic has not changed. What should the developer do?

options.text: Increase the maximum number of retries and the backoff ceiling so the job keeps trying longer.
options.why: This 429 is a spend cap, not a short-lived rate limit; access stays paused until the cap resets or is raised, so more retries only waste time.

options.text: Lower the job's concurrency so requests stay under the per-minute rate limits.
options.why: Traffic has not changed, and the error details show a spend cap rather than a requests- or tokens-per-minute limit.

options.text: Treat it as a spend cap: stop retrying, alert the owner, and raise the limit or wait for it to reset.
options.why: A 429 without retry-after that reports enforced_spend_limit_reached keeps failing until access resumes, so the recovery is a billing or limit change, not a retry.

options.text: Generate a new API key in the same organization and switch the job to it.
options.why: Spend caps and rate limits apply to the organization, so a new key in the same organization hits the same cap.

explanation: Error identification means reading more than the status code. Most 429s are temporary rate limits that carry retry-after and succeed after backing off. A 429 for a reached tier spend cap has no retry-after and keeps failing until access resumes, so retry logic should detect it, stop, and alert. A spend limit you set yourself returns a 400 invalid_request_error instead.
reference: Claude API docs — Rate limits (reaching your spend cap); Errors

stem: An agent loop sometimes ends with an empty reply. Traces show that each empty response has stop_reason "end_turn" and no content, and that it always follows a user message in which the app sends the tool_result block followed by a text block saying "Here is the tool output." Tool results themselves are correct. What should the developer change?

options.text: Retry the request unchanged whenever the reply is empty, up to three times.
options.why: Claude has already judged the turn complete from this history, so resending the same messages tends to produce the same empty result.

options.text: Send only the tool_result blocks in that user message, with no text block after them.
options.why: Text placed right after tool results teaches Claude to expect the user to speak next, so it ends its turn; removing it fixes the cause in the integration layer.

options.text: Raise max_tokens, because the model is running out of room before it can write the reply.
options.why: Running out of room is reported as stop_reason "max_tokens"; here Claude ended its turn deliberately with "end_turn".

options.text: Switch to a larger model, because the current one cannot interpret the tool output.
options.why: The trace points to how the app structures messages, not to model capability, and the same structure can trigger the behavior on any model.

explanation: Isolate the origin before choosing a fix. Here the tool output is correct and the pattern follows a specific message structure the app builds, so the defect is in the integration layer. The docs note that adding text blocks immediately after tool_result blocks can cause empty end_turn responses. If empty replies persist after fixing the structure, add a new user message asking Claude to continue rather than resending the same history.
reference: Claude API docs — Handling stop reasons (empty responses with end_turn)

stem: A Message Batch of 10,000 classification requests has ended. Results show 9,850 succeeded, 120 errored with invalid_request_error because the attached images are too large, and 30 errored with api_error. The job currently logs "batch complete" and moves on. What is the best recovery strategy?

options.text: Resubmit all 150 errored requests unchanged in a new batch and mark the job done once it is sent.
options.why: The 120 invalid requests will fail again until they are fixed, and marking the job done before they finish hides the gap.

options.text: Treat the whole batch as failed and resubmit all 10,000 requests so the results are consistent.
options.why: This throws away 9,850 good results, pays for them again, and still does not fix the 120 invalid requests.

options.text: Keep the 9,850 results and drop the 150 errored requests, since they are only 1.5% of the batch.
options.why: Silently dropping failures leaves records unprocessed with no signal to anyone, and most of them could be recovered.

options.text: Keep the successes, retry the 30 api_error requests, fix the 120 invalid ones, and report the gap.
options.why: Each error type gets its own recovery: transient errors are retried, invalid requests are corrected first, and the job reports what is still outstanding.

explanation: Batch results are per request: succeeded, errored, canceled or expired, matched by custom_id. Choose recovery by error type: an invalid_request_error must be fixed before resending, while a server error can be retried as is. Surface partial failures instead of reporting the batch as fully complete. Errored requests are not billed.
reference: Claude API docs — Batch processing (retrieving batch results)
